module_title: Phases of NISHTHA, DIKSHA Integration & Collaborative CPD
introduction: This intermediate tier details the specific phases of the NISHTHA program (1.0 to 4.0), explains how the DIKSHA portal acts as its delivery mechanism, and explores peer-driven Collaborative CPD through School Complexes.

core_concepts.title: The Evolution of NISHTHA (1.0 to 4.0)
core_concepts.description:
NISHTHA was rolled out in targeted phases to address specific educational stages:
- NISHTHA 1.0 (2019): Targeted Elementary level teachers (Classes 1 to 8). Originally face-to-face, later digitized.
- NISHTHA 2.0 (2021): Targeted Secondary level teachers (Classes 9 to 12).
- NISHTHA 3.0 (2021): Targeted Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN) under the NIPUN Bharat Mission (Ages 3-9).
- NISHTHA 4.0 (2022): Targeted Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) for Anganwadi workers and pre-primary teachers.

core_concepts.title: Delivery Mechanism: The DIKSHA Platform
core_concepts.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, NISHTHA transitioned from physical workshops to a completely online format hosted on the **DIKSHA** (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) platform. This allowed millions of teachers to complete their CPD modules asynchronously (at their own pace) and receive QR-coded digital certificates upon passing the objective assessments.

core_concepts.title: Professional Learning Communities (PLCs) & School Complexes
core_concepts.description:
NEP 2020 promotes the creation of 'School Complexes' (grouping a secondary school with smaller primary schools in a 5-10 km radius). 
- Within these complexes, teachers form PLCs. 
- Collaborative CPD: Instead of watching a video, teachers engage in peer-observation, co-planning lessons, and conducting collaborative Action Research to solve local pedagogical problems.

core_concepts.title: Multiple Modes of CPD
core_concepts.description:
A teacher can fulfill their 50-hour mandate through various recognized modes:
1. MOOCs (Massive Open Online Courses) on SWAYAM/DIKSHA.
2. Attending face-to-face workshops by DIETs/SCERTs.
3. Presenting research papers at educational conferences.
4. Peer-mentoring and collaborative lesson design.

important_entities.name: Action Research as CPD
important_entities.key_fact: The highest form of localized professional development.
important_entities.significance: When a teacher identifies a problem in their own classroom (e.g., 'Why do my students struggle with fractions?'), tests a new teaching method, records the data, and shares the findings with colleagues, this Action Research is officially recognized as a powerful, legitimate form of CPD.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse the two in exams. **DIKSHA** is the technological platform/app (the infrastructure). **NISHTHA** is the specific teacher training program/course that runs *on* the DIKSHA platform.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the rollout: It started in the middle (Elementary 1.0), moved up to Secondary (2.0), then went back to fix the foundation with FLN (3.0) and ECCE (4.0).

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks 'Which phase of NISHTHA was specifically launched to support the NIPUN Bharat Mission?', the correct answer is **NISHTHA 3.0 (FLN)**.
